fieldMarks: Medium-sized, pale lizard with a blunt head and a tail usually longer than the body (NDOW).
Darker lines and stripes run the length of the body and through the tail (NDOW).
behavior: Often one of the only lizards active in the hottest part of the day; among the most heat-tolerant reptiles in North America (NDOW).
Mostly eats leaves, buds and flowers, especially creosote bush, plus occasional insects and carrion (NDOW; NatureServe).
Shelters in rodent burrows, rock crevices or under creosote; when cornered wedges into a tight space and inflates its body (NDOW; NatureServe).
Mates April-May and lays 3-8 eggs June-August; inactive in cold weather (NatureServe).
habitat: Sandy arroyos and open areas with loose soil, typically creosote bush desert with sand hummocks and firm patches with scattered rocks; sometimes nearby rocky hillsides (NatureServe; NDOW).
range: Southern Nevada, southern California east of the Sierra Nevada and Coast ranges, and western and central Arizona south through Baja California and Sonora; United States range closely matches that of creosote bush; below sea level to about 1,520 m (NatureServe).
